market_scan.market_size_text: Same underlying pool as H9: mineral drying equipment+services is order-of-magnitude ~$1-3B/yr globally inside a ~$5-10B industrial dryer market, with minerals/ores ~24% of rotary dryer demand. The capacity-booster angle targets the installed base rather than new lines: dryers run 20-40 years, replacement/upgrade is a named demand driver in market reports, and OEM aftermarket/service is ~30-40% of dryer-OEM revenue (~). A new large rotary line costs ~$8-15M installed with 12-18-month lead times, so a retrofit that adds ~20-30% throughput for low single-digit $M addresses a real capex-avoidance budget — adjacent precedents exist (microwave boost ovens +25% throughput in food; IR booster sections debottlenecking paper machines; parallel fluid-bed additions at a 48->100 ktpa magnesium plant).

regions.Europe: ~$0.3-0.7B (aging installed base + ETS pressure; retrofit-friendly, capex-constrained mid-size producers)
regions.Asia: ~$1-2B (largest market but dominated by new-build/greenfield; retrofit slice smaller share)
regions.America: ~$0.5-1.2B (large aging fleet; debottlenecking culture strong in NA minerals/mining)
regions.Africa: ~$0.1-0.3B (mine expansions; often cheaper to overbuild new than retrofit)

market_scan.target_customers_text: Operators whose drying step limits line throughput — typically because feed moisture rose (wetter ore, seasonal stockpiles), demand grew, or the dryer aged. Same base as H9: ~750 IMA-member processing plants in Europe, majors like Omya (~160 plants) and Imerys (~100+ sites) centralizing engineering decisions, plus hundreds of ore concentrators running single-line dryers where +10-20% capacity has high marginal value against $8-15M for a parallel line. Reachable through dryer-OEM aftermarket channels, plant engineering managers, and industry consultants; buying trigger is a capacity project already being scoped, so timing windows are episodic but the value case (avoided capex + deferred permitting) is concrete.
market_scan.players_text: Conventional debottlenecking is served by the incumbent dryer OEMs' aftermarket arms (Metso, FLSmidth, Andritz, ThyssenKrupp, GEA) selling upgrades, heat-recovery retrofits (~18-25% fuel savings reported in EU cement/mineral retrofits) and parallel units, plus mid-tier OEMs doing add-on dryers. Booster/inline technology is a niche: microwave boost ovens proven in food (Ferrite/IMS MIP-9, +25% throughput), IR booster sections proven in paper/board (Ircon Solaronics), but no established microwave-booster player for bulk minerals — whitespace similar to H9.

regulation: Debottlenecking by adding gas-fired capacity increases ETS exposure (~EUR60-90/tCO2); an electric booster adds throughput with zero on-site combustion.
Uprating burners or adding combustion capacity can trigger permit modification and tighter emission limits; an electric booster avoids reopening combustion permitting.
Increased firing rates on existing dryers can trigger New Source Review/BACT analysis; non-combustion boosters sidestep it.
Mandatory energy audits push operators to exploit low-capex efficiency/capacity measures — a booster that raises output per GJ is a natural audit action.
National decarbonization funding (DE EEW, EU Innovation Fund, US IRA 48C/DOE)
Retrofit projects combining capacity gain with electrification qualify for process-heat decarbonization subsidies, improving booster economics.

technologies.name: Existing rotary/fluid-bed/flash dryer (the asset to boost)
technologies.how: Fossil-fired drum, fluid bed or flash tube whose throughput is set by evaporation duty (kJ per kg water) and residence time.
technologies.performance: ~1.0-2.5 kWh_th/kg water; single lines 20-100+ t/h; dryers routinely the plant bottleneck when inlet moisture or demand rises.
technologies.limits: Capacity is thermally capped: more feed needs more burner + air handling + permit headroom; drum length/diameter fixes residence time.

technologies.name: Upstream mechanical dewatering (filter press, centrifuge, screen)
technologies.how: Remove free water mechanically before thermal drying — cheapest water removal (~1/10 the energy of thermal).
technologies.performance: Cuts filter-cake moisture to ~8-15% for concentrates; classic first debottleneck step.
technologies.limits: Cannot reach low residual moisture; not applicable to already-granular/free-draining ores and sands that enter the dryer at 5-12%.

technologies.name: Parallel/second dryer line (conventional debottleneck)
technologies.how: Install an additional rotary or fluid-bed dryer alongside the existing one.
technologies.performance: Hatch magnesium project: tripled fluid-bed dryer count to go 48->100 ktpa. New large rotary line ~$8-15M installed, 12-18-month lead.
technologies.limits: Full capex, footprint, ducting/fans/baghouse duplicated, combustion permit and ETS exposure grow; outage and tie-in complexity.

technologies.name: Heat-recovery / indirect-heat retrofit
technologies.how: Exhaust-gas heat exchangers, insulation, burner upgrades, conversion to indirect heating to free thermal margin.
technologies.performance: EU cement/mineral retrofits report ~18-25% fuel reduction; recovers capacity margin indirectly.
technologies.limits: Raises throughput only modestly (~5-15%); engineering downtime; still fossil-fired.

technologies.name: Inline booster drying sections (IR/hot-air) — proven in paper
technologies.how: Compact high-intensity IR or air dryers inserted at bottleneck points of an existing line to add evaporation without rebuild.
technologies.performance: Ircon Solaronics references: removes line bottlenecks, lifts machine speed/capacity without full rebuilds; standard practice in paper/board.
technologies.limits: Surface heating suits webs/sheets, not deep mineral beds; mineral analog largely unproven.

technologies.name: Microwave pre-dryer / booster (ProSeed)
technologies.how: 915/2450 MHz tunnel upstream (or interstage) of the existing dryer strips the constant-rate moisture load volumetrically; the incumbent dryer only finishes to spec.
technologies.performance: Food analog MIP-9 boost ovens: +25% throughput at 75-300 kW per tunnel; mineral pilots show MW drying 6-13x faster and -30-50% energy vs convective, so a few-hundred-kW to ~1 MW booster can offload ~20-40% of evaporation duty.
technologies.limits: Abrasive, high-temperature mineral belt/applicator design unproven at scale; dielectric response varies by matrix (silica poor, iron ore good); adds ~kWh_el operating cost vs gas unless efficiency + carbon economics compensate.

tech_baseline.why_better_text: A microwave booster adds evaporation capacity in meters of tunnel, not tens of meters of drum: volumetric water-selective heating removes part of the load upstream so the existing dryer finishes faster — the same +25-30% throughput effect proven by MW boost ovens in food and IR boosters in paper. It installs in a short outage at a fraction of the $8-15M and 12-18 months of a parallel line, adds no burner so no permit or ETS expansion, and its instant controllability also fixes moisture-uniformity problems that often are the true throughput limiter. For capacity-constrained plants the value is avoided capex plus earlier tonnes, not energy savings per se.
key_assumptions: Drying is frequently the bottleneck when feed moisture or demand rises; upstream boosting gives +20-30% line throughput — proven for MW in food (MIP-9, measured) and IR in paper (measured); transfer to mineral beds assumed.
Offloading ~2-4 percentage points of inlet moisture upstream removes ~20-40% of the existing dryer's evaporation duty (assumed; depends on inlet moisture profile).
New parallel rotary line: ~$8-15M installed, 12-18-month lead (measured, market/capex references); a MW booster line est. <$1-3M per ~1 MW installed (assumed).
Mineral duty (abrasion, 100-300C, dust) requires new applicator/belt engineering — the main technical risk, plus dielectric-loss variability by mineral (measured spread 40-78% drying efficiency).

Booster opex: ~0.7-1.0 kWh_el/kg water removed vs ~1.2-2.0 kWh_th/kg in the incumbent; at EU industrial power ~EUR60-100/MWh vs gas ~EUR30-50/MWh, opex is roughly neutral-to-better while throughput is the payback driver (assumed).
